title: SKU-aware wake scheduler for prefill/decode on H100, L40S, A10
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a SKU-aware 'wake scheduler' that coordinates prefill and decode workloads across H100, L40S and A10 devices (including MIG partitions). The scheduler combines a short-horizon burst predictor, a hardware capability vector, and a kernel scoring function to decide: 1) when to start prefill for a request to reduce p95 tail, 2) which kernel variant to pick (fused attention vs. sequence-sliced) given current clocks/MIGing, and 3) whether to pin workload to a specific MIG slice or fall back to cross-slice execution. Goal: reduce p95 latency for mixed synchronous workloads by 20–30% and reduce unnecessary clock ramping/burn for low-density request patterns.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Nightly benchmark shows >=15% p95 improvement for mixed length workloads on H100 and >=10% on L40S and A10 for the PL-and-PL+prefill scenarios; 2) No more than 5% regressed throughput for high-throughput batch workloads; 3) Telemetry surfaces SKU and MIG-level kernel choices per-request; 4) Feature gated and toggled via runtime-config; 5) Rollout plan documented with safe fallback to existing scheduler.
design_notes:
Core components:
- Burst predictor: lightweight LRU-based estimator using per-route inter-arrival statistics + token-length histogram to predict short (200–800ms) bursts.
- Hardware capability vector: per-device properties (SM count, DDR bandwidth estimate, clock headroom heuristic, MIG slices present, microkernel availability).
- Kernel scoring: score = latency_estimate * alpha + energy_penalty * beta + clock_hysteresis_penalty * gamma. Scores precomputed for common (seq_len, batch_size) pairs and refreshed on clock/temperature hysteresis events.
- Wake scheduler policy: decide prefill lead-time (ms) to start KV population so that critical tokens hit warm KV cache without spinning up clocks unnecessarily. Lead-time tuned per-SKU and per-MIG slice size.
- MIG-awareness: prefer warming an occupied MIG slice if affinity exists; consider cross-slice packing only if predicted batch density requires it.
- Clock governor integration: consult node-level governor to avoid frequent DVFS swings; if kernel scoring suggests higher clocks but clock hysteresis penalty outweighs latency gain, choose a kernel that prefers lower clock efficiency (e.g., multi-stage attention that trades cycles for memory locality).
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 wks): telemetry + scoring data collection. Add per-request kernel hint metadata and route-level IA histograms.
Phase 2 (3 wks): implement burst predictor and offline calibration jobs to generate initial score tables per SKU.
Phase 3 (2 wks): integrate wake scheduler into runtime admission path with feature flag; unit tests + microbench harness.
Phase 4 (2 wks): limited Canary rollout to 10% of dedicated capacity across H100 and L40S pools.
Phase 5 (2 wks): analyze telemetry, iterate scoring weights, expand to A10 pools and MIG configurations.
Phase 6: full rollout with postmortem and docs.
experiments_and_metrics:
Key metrics: request p50/p95/p99 latency (prefill and decode phases), tokens/sec per-GPU, GPU clock change frequency, percentage of requests that triggered a prefill, fraction of kernels chosen (fused vs sliced), thermal throttling incidents.
Experiment buckets: control (current scheduler), SKU-only (no MIG-awareness), SKU+MIG (full scheduler).
Success thresholds: SKU+MIG must beat control on p95 with <5% throughput loss and reduce clock-change frequency by >=25% in low-rate workloads.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Burst predictor false positives increase unnecessary prefill and clock ramp leading to higher power; mitigation: conservative default thresholds, chargeback telemetry and auto-disable when power increases >5%.
Risk: Complex kernel scoring table bloat across SKUs/MIG sizes; mitigation: quantize sequence lengths and cache top-K scores, fallback to generic kernel heuristics.
Risk: Regression on heavy batch workloads; mitigation: staged rollout, real-time rollback flag in console, and integration test with synthetic high-batch traces.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged binary released to runtime nodes (disabled by default).
2) Enable telemetry-only mode for 3 days to collect real-world scoring inputs.
3) Enable scheduler on test pool + small canary (5–10% traffic) for 1 week with close monitoring.
4) Expand to Dedicated H100/L40S pools then A10; keep MIG configurations small during first 2 weeks.
5) Full enable with ack from reliability and infra teams.
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel scoring and clock penalty math, integration tests using local GPU nodes (H100, L40S, A10 emulation), and perf harness replaying production traces with annotated MIG topologies. Add end-to-end Canary acceptance checks: no p95 regression and clock-change frequency decrease on low-rate traffic.
